explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem only unfolds the library's own definitions. `coordinateRingToPolynomialQuotient` is defined as `Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (determinantOneIdeal K n) (localizationToPolynomialQuotient K n) _`, and `quotient` is defined as `Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K (determinantOneIdeal K n)`. The proof applies Mathlib's `Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ_comp`, but that lemma is the generic universal property of the quotient: a lift composed with the quotient map gives back the original map. This is the same kind of structural lemma as `lift_comp_mk`, applied to the library's own maps. It falls under the "general principles applied to the library's own definitions" exclusion, because all the mathematical content (the maps `localizationToPolynomialQuotient` and `coordinateRingToPolynomialQuotient`) comes from the library. So it is neither a duplicate nor a special case.
